clue.text: Police unit will be involved in action for certain

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so the unit sits within the action

blocks.note: a deed is an act or action
the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Someone insists a detective squad will definitely get involved in a police operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For certain' looks like one phrase, but 'for' only joins and 'certain' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A decided matter is settled and beyond doubt, the adjectival sense of certain.

clue.text: Beer with dirt tossed on top is well stupid

indicators.note: something tossed over is flipped, so in a down answer the word is read upwards
in a down clue, being on top means coming first, above the other piece

blocks.note: mud is wet dirt
Bass is a well-known English brand of ale

explanation.surface: Someone who throws dirt on top of a pint is being very silly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass is a well-known English ale. 'Well' is British slang for 'very', so 'well stupid' means very stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbass is slang for an idiot, used as an adjective for a person who is extremely foolish.

clue.text: Socialist that's firm about statement of principles

indicators.note: about means around, so the firm's abbreviation wraps the socialist

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
red is the traditional colour, and nickname, of the left

explanation.surface: A left-wing company issues a statement setting out its values.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo, Latin for 'I believe', is a set of beliefs or guiding principles.

clue.text: Insult 51 in complaint is 'an inability to accept the truth'

definitions.text: an inability to accept the truth

indicators.note: the number is placed in the complaint, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to dis someone is slang for to insult them
a beef is slang for a grievance
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A quoted definition, as though someone's grievance about an insult shows they cannot face facts.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the definition look like a quoted phrase within the surface; the number is Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief is the refusal or failure to credit something as real.

clue.text: Oxbridge professor is a gentleman from Spain

blocks.note: first meaning: a senior academic at Oxford or Cambridge
second meaning: the Spanish title of respect for a man

explanation.surface: A Cambridge academic turns out to be a Spanish nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is both the term for a fellow of an Oxbridge college and the Spanish honorific for a gentleman.

clue.text: Religious basket case?

blocks.note: surface reading: a person driven crazy by religious zeal
setter's reading: a biblical baby found floating in a basket of reeds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Basket case' is slang for someone unhinged, but here it means a case involving a literal basket: the infant hidden among the bulrushes in Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the prophet was set adrift as a baby in a papyrus basket on the Nile.

clue.text: Maiden getting beers for blokes

blocks.note: M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A young woman fetches drinks for the lads.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is British slang for a man, so blokes are men in general.

clue.text: One who'd accept everything was well or fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gullible person reports everything was fine or even marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: To swallow a story is to believe it without question.
explanation.definitionFit: A swallower here is a credulous person who believes whatever they are told.

clue.text: Enough drink to get drunk is wrong in God's eyes, king held

indicators.note: something held is gripped within, so the monarch sits inside the other word

blocks.note: sinful means morally wrong by religious law
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A preacher says drinking to excess is sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: K goes after the S of SINFUL, giving S-K-INFUL. A skinful is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Having had a skinful means having drunk enough alcohol to be intoxicated.

clue.text: Terribly solemn pair might be frigid

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A very serious couple might come across as cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a cold manner lacking personal warmth.

clue.text: Hoskins must tuck into a shot for a fee

indicators.note: to tuck into something is to slip inside it

blocks.note: a go is an attempt, a shot
the setter refers to themselves, so I

explanation.surface: The setter must have a go to earn a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into A GO. Setters often use their own pseudonym to mean I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An agio is a charge made for exchanging currency, a banking fee.

clue.text: One who purposely wrecks boat sure must change

indicators.note: the letters must change their order to form a new word

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who deliberately damages a boat is sure to have to alter their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur is a person who deliberately damages property or plans.

clue.text: Special gear and excellent beer from the rear

indicators.note: reading from the rear means starting at the end and working back

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A list of good things: fancy clothes and fine beer drunk from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: AI and LAGER together are read backwards to give REGALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the ceremonial robes and insignia worn on formal occasions, a special outfit.

clue.text: Flips out, inhaling fourth of puffs from this?

definitions.text: Flips out, inhaling fourth of puffs from this?

indicators.note: a word that flips out goes wild, so its letters are rearranged
fourth of tells us to take only the letter in fourth position
inhaling means drawing something in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the fourth letter of puffs

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy after taking a drag: could this be the cause?
explanation.walkthrough: FLIPS rearranged to SPLIF takes in F before its last letter. The whole clue also describes the effect of smoking one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is a cannabis cigarette, something one inhales and that might make one flip.

clue.text: American husband hugged by short relative is a dish

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter
something hugged by another is held within its arms

blocks.note: sis is short for sister, a relative
US is the abbreviation for American
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A US husband embraced by his little sister is a real catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the relative's height; it cuts the word down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese food of vinegared rice with raw fish, served as a dish.

clue.text: Totally demolish small Snickers?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
snickers are stifled laughs, a kind of laughter

explanation.surface: It reads like smashing a little chocolate bar, Snickers being a brand of candy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Snickers look like the chocolate bar; it is the noun for sniggers.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter an opponent is to defeat them overwhelmingly, to demolish them.

clue.text: Gloomy and down about female being beastly!

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: the clue treats the answer as a beast

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: grey weather or moods are gloomy
low means feeling down
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman who is miserable and depressed is behaving terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'beastly' hints that the answer is an animal rather than giving a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey wolf is a wild beast, the largest member of the dog family.

clue.text: Online career for life in induction

blocks.note: E as in e-mail stands for electronic, online
a vocation is a calling, a lifelong career

explanation.surface: Someone finds a lifelong internet career during their job orientation.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocation is the calling forth of a feeling or image, as induction brings about a state.

clue.text: Returned mutt with odd flaw that's bitten you? Terrible!

indicators.note: something returned is sent back, so the word is read backwards
odd means strange, so the letters are put into an unusual order
the jumbled word bites and so holds the other piece in its jaws

blocks.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
the letters to be rearranged
U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A dog brought back from the pound has a strange fault and has bitten you: dreadful!
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of the fault wrap the letter for you before joining the reversed mutt.
explanation.definitionFit: Godawful is an intensified form of awful, meaning extremely bad.

clue.text: Your lad cycling as the Virgin Mary

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the first letter moves round to the end

blocks.note: the letters to be cycled

explanation.surface: A son pedals along, dressed up as the mother of Jesus in a nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y moves from the front of YOURLAD to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Lady is the title Catholics and others give to the mother of Jesus.

clue.text: Those starting on good religious evangelists seem monsters

indicators.note: those starting are the letters that begin each of the following words

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Starting out as preachers, these people come across as frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folk tales, monsters.

clue.text: Drunk now and you can't do anything about it!

definitions.text: you can't do anything about it!

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
here can mean at this point, now

explanation.surface: A defiant boozer says they are drunk right now and nobody can stop them.
explanation.definitionFit: So there is a defiant retort meaning the matter is settled and the listener is powerless.

clue.text: Old Republican leader with inflated self-worth ultimately in state

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
first letter of Republican
an inflated ego is an overblown sense of one's own importance
last letter of in

explanation.surface: A former Republican party leader with an inflated sense of himself ends up in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In state' looks like 'in a state of'; 'in' is the source of the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a US state on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Ultimate of owl-haters in People Against Hooters

indicators.note: the ultimate of a word is its very last letter
one piece is placed in another, inside it

blocks.note: the noes are those who vote against
last letter of owl-haters

explanation.surface: It reads like a campaign group of people who hate owls, the birds that hoot.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes in NOES. 'Hooter' is British slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooter is slang for the nose, so hooters are noses.

clue.text: Liqueur excessive queen and a mother knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: OTT is short for over the top, excessive
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A queen and her mother overdo it, downing an almond liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, ER, A and MA are read backwards together. 'Knocked back' also suggests downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Old head of state will cuddle tense man? Heavens!

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap one's arms round, so these pieces are held inside

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A former queen hugs a nervous man, to cries of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark disguises 'Heavens' as an oath; it means the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether is a poetic word for the upper sky, the heavens.

clue.text: Bolt double? That's what one might be aiming for!

definitions.text: double? That's what one might be aiming for!
definitions.note: a cryptic description rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: to dash or move suddenly

blocks.clueFragment: double? That's what one might be aiming for!
blocks.note: second meaning: what a player throws when aiming at a double ring on the board

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt double' reads like a lookalike of the sprinter Usain Bolt; the double is the outer ring scoring twice on a dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly, and a dart is the missile a darts player aims at a double.

clue.text: Make neat gin hatter will mix with drop of soda

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters are jumbled
a drop is a small amount, here just the opening letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
first letter of soda

explanation.surface: A hatter makes a neat gin into a mixed drink with a dash of soda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat gin' looks like undiluted spirit, but 'Make neat' is the definition and 'gin' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten a room is to tidy it, to make it orderly.

clue.text: Coastal inlet found in Cagliari area

indicators.note: found in says the letters are discovered inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A sea inlet can be seen in the region around Cagliari, the capital of Sardinia.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow inlet formed by the sea flooding a river valley.

clue.text: Operative retreating around soldiers in battle

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
around means surrounding, so the soldiers are put inside

blocks.note: an operative is a secret agent
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: An agent falls back as soldiers surround him during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: SPY read backwards is YPS, which then takes in RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres in Belgium was the site of several major First World War battles.

clue.text: Perhaps pine to get to end of a popular racecourse

indicators.note: getting to the end of something means being placed after it

blocks.note: taken as written
in means fashionable, popular
a pine is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: Someone longs to reach the finish at a well-loved racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the verb to long for; it is the tree. Aintree near Liverpool hosts the Grand National horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous English horse racing venue, home of the Grand National.
